steps.title: Bordeaux
steps.body: In Bordeaux, Sauvignon Blanc is blended with Sémillon, sometimes Muscadelle. Sauvignon brings acidity and aroma; Sémillon body and texture. Pessac-Léognan makes the finest dry whites, often fermented and aged in oak, which can age 20 years. Entre-Deux-Mers makes fresh, unoaked versions. Sauvignon is also part of sweet Sauternes.

steps.title: Fumé Blanc
steps.body: In 1966, Robert Mondavi in California named his oak-aged Sauvignon Blanc Fumé Blanc, borrowing from Pouilly-Fumé, to sell a then-unpopular grape. It worked. Today Fumé Blanc in the US often, but not always, means an oaked Sauvignon. The term isn't legally defined.

steps.prompt: Who created the name Fumé Blanc?

steps.title: Sweet and other styles
steps.body: In Sauternes, Sauvignon adds acidity and freshness to botrytised Sémillon. In Styria, Austria, and Friuli, Italy, Sauvignon is made in a mineral, sometimes oak-aged style. Chile's Leyda and South Africa's Elgin give fresh, coastal versions.

steps.prompt: Fumé Blanc is a legally defined style.
steps.explanation: Not true. It's a marketing term, often but not always meaning an oaked Sauvignon.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Bordeaux blends Sauvignon with Sémillon, often oaked
Fumé Blanc was Mondavi's 1966 marketing name
